title: Blackhole Tracker: BHSM Boundary Interpretation of Compact-Lens Mass, Motion, and Conditional Response

authors.name: Norman P. Carberry
authors.provenance: Established author facts reused under the user's current instruction 'Thats it, the same as always'; contact and identity recovered by coordinating agent from preserved manuscripts.

abstract: Blackhole Tracker provides reproducible lens inference with explicit Berger–Hopf Standard Model (BHSM) interpretation: one effective exterior is counted once. A local app, command line, Python package and notebooks support resolved image-pair data and native unresolved-photometry likelihood. An internally frozen pilot processes 100 OGLE-III events and 76\,344 measurements. Eighty-nine fail the specified photometric adequacy screen; eleven are not rejected; two pass stricter archival follow-up criteria. Both are published events. Their timescales do not identify mass, distance or absolute motion; no new black-hole interpretation is established. A 2022 benchmark rejects rectilinear photometry-only fits. A separately versioned joint benchmark uses 12\,521 photometric measurements and 21 two-coordinate HST positions. Three frozen noise candidates converge but fail residual-structure checks; their masses remain conditional. Earlier resolved-pair synthetic calibrations remain separately versioned. Reviewed corrections remove numerical-reference dependence, admit physical nuisance profiles and preserve unavailable motion uncertainties. The optional scalar–tensor calculation bounds boundary states in its retained exterior, but two projected modes vanish and the leading apparent-mass response is degenerate with shear. The software supports auditable event screening and conditional response tests. Neither BHSM core dynamics, a detectable envelope, nor a horizon classification is measured by these observations.
